questions.stem: In the context of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the roles of various functionaries involved, consider the following statements. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Form 7, used during the Claims and Objections phase, is meant to object to the inclusion of a name in the electoral roll or to seek deletion of an entry.
A Booth Level Agent (BLA) is a statutory functionary appointed by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
The Booth Level Officer (BLO) is appointed by political parties to independently monitor the revision of electoral rolls in a constituency.
An application seeking deletion of a voter's name from the electoral roll does not require the signature of the elector or the objecting applicant.
questions.explanation: Only statement 1 is correct. A BLA is appointed by a political party, not by the ECI, so it is not a statutory functionary; the BLO is in fact appointed by the Electoral Registration Officer, not by political parties; and the very controversy reported (pre-printed Form 7s without applicant signatures) shows that a signature is mandatorily required, making statement 4 false.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Telangana SIR: BLOs being forced to accept Form-7s without signature of applicants
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory process of electoral roll revision under the Representation of the People Act, 1950 (Forms 6/7/8, BLO/BLA/ERO roles) — a recurring Polity PYQ theme on the Election Commission's machinery.

questions.stem: With reference to the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) and its policy instruments, consider the following statements. How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI consists of six members, with the RBI Governor serving as its Chairperson.
The Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate is normally fixed above the repo rate and acts as the ceiling of the liquidity adjustment facility corridor.
Under its statutory inflation-targeting mandate, the RBI is required to keep CPI inflation within a band of 2% to 6%, with 4% as the mid-point target.
A shift in monetary policy stance from 'neutral' to 'calibrated tightening' signals the central bank's intent to cut interest rates further in the near term.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The SDF rate is actually fixed below the repo rate and forms the floor, not the ceiling, of the LAF corridor — confirmed by the article's figures (repo 5.50%, SDF 5.25%); and a 'calibrated tightening' stance signals further rate hikes or a prolonged pause, not cuts.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Rising inflation risks push RBI to raise repo rate by 25 bps to 5.50%
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional design of the MPC and the inflation-targeting framework under the amended RBI Act, 1934 — similar to UPSC 2021's question on expansionary monetary policy tools.

questions.stem: With reference to the Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Purchasing Managers' Index tracking India's services and manufacturing activity is compiled by S&P Global, with HSBC sponsoring the survey.
A PMI reading of 50 or above indicates a contraction in economic activity compared to the previous month.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct, as the article explicitly describes the 'HSBC India Services PMI, compiled by S&P Global.' Statement 2 reverses the standard interpretation — a reading above 50 signals expansion, not contraction, while a reading below 50 indicates contraction.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: India's services sector growth hits three-month high: PMI survey
questions.pyqLink: Tests the basic construction and interpretation of a private economic indicator (PMI), a recurring static-current fusion theme in Economy prelims questions.

questions.stem: With reference to the GST Council, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The GST Council was constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution, inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
The Union Finance Minister serves as the Chairperson of the GST Council, with the finance ministers of states as its members.
Decisions of the GST Council are taken by a simple majority of members present and voting, with the Centre and all states together having equal voting weightage of 50% each.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct descriptions of the GST Council's constitutional basis and composition. Statement 3 is incorrect: Council decisions require a three-fourths majority of weighted votes cast, with the Centre holding one-third weightage and all states together holding two-thirds — not a simple 50-50 majority.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: GST Council aims to ease compliance, expedite refunds, curb frequent rate tweaks
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279A and the GST Council's voting mechanism, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on cooperative federalism bodies.

pairs: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
HSBC India Services Purchasing Managers' Index

The fourth pair is wrong — the Wholesale Price Index is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (Ministry of Commerce), not the RBI.

questions.sourceTitle: Govt plans to expand services index to cover 80% of sector output
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional ownership of key economic indices, a format UPSC 2023 used heavily for 'reports and publishing bodies' pairs questions.

questions.stem: The sacrifice of Tiruppur Kumaran in January 1932 occurred against the backdrop of the resumption of a major phase of the national movement. Which one of the following best describes the Civil Disobedience Movement?
options: A movement launched by the Indian National Congress in 1942 demanding immediate British withdrawal from India, accompanied by the call to 'Do or Die'.
A nationwide campaign of deliberate, non-violent defiance of specific British laws, including salt and prohibitory laws, resumed by Gandhi after the breakdown of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
A purely constitutional movement seeking dominion status for India solely through participation in the Round Table Conferences, without any element of law-breaking.
An agitation confined to the non-payment of land revenue in Gujarat, led by Vallabhbhai Patel.
questions.explanation: Option b correctly describes the Civil Disobedience Movement, which Gandhi resumed in January 1932 after Viceroy Willingdon abandoned the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and reverted to repression — the exact context in which Tiruppur Kumaran's sacrifice occurred. Option a describes the Quit India Movement of 1942; option c wrongly denies the movement's law-breaking character; option d describes the narrower Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Tiruppur Kumaran: a sacrifice that defied the British Raj
questions.pyqLink: Tests the defining features and chronology of the Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34), a staple History PYQ theme distinguishing it from Non-Cooperation and Quit India movements.

questions.stem: Consider the following two statements regarding India's crude oil security.
statements: Statement-I: India's crude oil supply is highly exposed to disruptions in West Asia, since a majority of its crude oil, LNG and LPG imports before the recent conflict were sourced from that region.

Statement-II: The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow maritime chokepoint connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, through which a large share of the world's seaborne crude oil trade passes.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. The article confirms about 50% of India's crude oil, 54% of LNG, and 90% of LPG imports were sourced from West Asia and routed through the Strait of Hormuz; Statement-II correctly explains why this geography creates supply vulnerability, since the Strait is the chokepoint through which this trade must physically pass, making Statement-II the valid explanation for Statement-I.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Iran war: Shell sees Middle East oil flows at 80% as Saudi Aramco warns inventories may take 2 years to rebuild
questions.pyqLink: Tests the physical and economic geography of global oil chokepoints, a theme UPSC has tested via 'international straits/chokepoints in the news' map-based and statement questions.

questions.stem: With reference to the Election Commission of India, consider the following statements, in the context of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls:
statements: Statement-I: The Election Commission of India has the constitutional authority to order a Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
Statement-II: Article 324 of the Constitution vests in the Election Commission of India the power of superintendence, direction and control of elections, including the preparation of electoral rolls.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Article 324 gives the ECI overarching superintendence over elections, which is the constitutional source of its power to direct revisions of electoral rolls under the Representation of the People Act, 1950. Both statements are factually correct, and Statement-II is precisely the constitutional basis that explains Statement-I, so it is the correct explanation.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: CEC row LIVE: CJP's Saurav Das to submit 'intimation letter' to Delhi Police ahead of October 10 Jantar Mantar protest; security tightened
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 324 (ECI's powers of superintendence, direction and control of elections); similar to UPSC's recurring Statement-I/II pattern on constitutional bodies since 2022

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the GST Council, ahead of its meeting on October 8:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: It is a constitutional body headed by the Union Finance Minister.
It was constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution, inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
Its decisions are binding on both the Union and the States and cannot be deviated from by either.
The Union Finance Minister alone casts the deciding vote in the Council, with States having no voting rights.
questions.explanation: The GST Council is indeed a constitutional body under Article 279A (101st Amendment, 2016) chaired by the Union Finance Minister, so the first two statements are correct. The Supreme Court in Union of India v. Mohit Minerals (2022) held that GST Council recommendations are only recommendatory, not binding, making the third statement false; voting is weighted (Centre 1/3, States collectively 2/3 of votes cast) and not a Centre-only decision, making the fourth statement false too.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Centre to propose five-pronged reform plan at GST Council meeting on October 8
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 279A and the binding/recommendatory nature of GST Council decisions (Mohit Minerals verdict); similar to UPSC 2022 cooperative federalism/GST questions

questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correctly matched: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (India's first, notified 1986) spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka; Sundarbans lies in West Bengal; Great Nicobar is in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; and Achanakmar-Amarkantak straddles Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. The Nilgiris connection comes from the Keystone Foundation's bee-conservation work in the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve referenced in the news.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: When Raajadharshini captured the queen (bees) of the Nilgiris

questions.stem: A tusker in Keralam died after being struck by lightning during a thunderstorm. With reference to the atmospheric phenomenon of lightning, which one of the following best describes its formation?
options: Collisions between ice crystals and soft hail (graupel) within cumulonimbus clouds cause charge separation, which is neutralised through a sudden electrical discharge.
Friction between stratus clouds and rising warm air currents during the retreating monsoon generates the electrical charge that produces lightning.
Positively charged ions from the ionosphere discharge directly toward negatively charged particles accumulated at the Earth's surface.
The piezoelectric effect generated by hailstones falling through the troposphere is the accepted mechanism for lightning formation.
questions.explanation: Lightning forms inside tall cumulonimbus clouds when collisions between rising ice crystals and falling graupel separate charge, building up a strong electric field that discharges as lightning. Stratus clouds are low, stable clouds not associated with thunderstorms; the ionosphere plays no direct role in cloud-to-ground lightning; and the piezoelectric effect is not the scientifically accepted mechanism.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Tusker Pallatt Brahmadathan dies after lightning strike near Erattupetta in Keralam’s Kottayam
questions.pyqLink: Tests the physics of thunderstorm electrification and cumulonimbus cloud formation, a recurring UPSC theme on atmospheric phenomena and disaster-related science

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Thrissur Pooram festival and the institution of Devaswom Boards in Keralam:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Thrissur Pooram is held at the Guruvayur Temple, which also houses Keralam's largest elephant sanctuary.
Devaswom Boards are statutory bodies responsible for managing the administration and properties of Hindu temples in Keralam.
'Musth' is a periodic physiological condition in male elephants marked by heightened aggression and elevated testosterone levels.
Thrissur Pooram is jointly organised every year by the Thiruvambadi Devaswom and the Paramekkavu Devaswom.
questions.explanation: Thrissur Pooram is actually held at the Vadakkunnathan Temple, not the Guruvayur Temple (which is a separate shrine famous for its elephant sanctuary), making the first statement false. Devaswom Boards are indeed statutory bodies managing Kerala's temples, musth is correctly described as a male elephant condition with heightened aggression, and the festival is correctly attributed to the Thiruvambadi and Paramekkavu Devaswoms, making the remaining three statements correct.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Tusker Pallattu Brahmadathan, who died in a lightning strike, cremated in Keralam
questions.pyqLink: Tests temple-management institutions (Devaswom Boards) and festival traditions of Kerala, a recurring art-and-culture theme in Prelims

questions.stem: With reference to the Southwest Monsoon and its effect on Tamil Nadu's climate, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Tamil Nadu receives the bulk of its annual rainfall from the Northeast (retreating) monsoon rather than the Southwest monsoon, because the Western Ghats block southwest monsoon winds before they reach much of the State.
The Southwest monsoon over India is driven by the seasonal reversal of winds caused by differential heating of land and the surrounding oceans.
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats act as an orographic barrier, creating a rain-shadow effect over most of Tamil Nadu during the Southwest monsoon, so the State depends more on the Northeast monsoon for its rainfall, making the first statement correct. The Southwest monsoon is indeed driven by differential heating between landmass and ocean causing seasonal wind reversal, making the second statement correct as well.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: T.N. records highest Southwest monsoon temperatures in the last nine years
questions.pyqLink: Tests the mechanism of the Southwest Monsoon and the rain-shadow effect of the Western Ghats on Tamil Nadu, a classic Indian physical geography theme

questions.stem: With reference to international civil aviation, in the context of the slot-allocation dispute at Mumbai's Terminal 2 affecting foreign carriers such as Emirates and Etihad Airways, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) directly allocates airport slots to individual airlines operating international routes.
The allocation of international flight slots and traffic rights between India and foreign countries is governed by Bilateral Air Services Agreements (ASAs).
The Ministry of Civil Aviation is the nodal ministry responsible for negotiating Air Services Agreements on behalf of India.
questions.explanation: ICAO sets global technical and safety standards but does not itself allocate airport slots to airlines; slot allocation is done by national/airport-level slot coordinators under guidelines such as the IATA Worldwide Slot Guidelines, making the first statement false. Traffic rights between countries are indeed governed by Bilateral Air Services Agreements, and India's Ministry of Civil Aviation is the nodal authority that negotiates these agreements, making the second and third statements correct.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Centre intervenes to buy airlines more time at Adani’s Mumbai airport
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional framework of Bilateral Air Services Agreements and the distinction between ICAO's standard-setting role and national slot allocation

questions.stem: With reference to the Indian economy, which one of the following best describes the term 'Merchant Discount Rate (MDR)'?
options: It is the rate of interest charged by banks on cash credit accounts extended to merchants for working capital needs
It is a fee charged to a merchant by a bank or payment system operator for accepting payments through digital instruments such as cards or UPI
It is a discount that merchants voluntarily offer to customers who choose to pay through digital modes instead of cash
It is a statutory ceiling fixed by the Reserve Bank of India on interest charged on loans extended to merchants under priority sector lending
questions.explanation: MDR is the fee a merchant pays the acquiring bank/payment system operator for processing a digital transaction; NPCI is set to operationalise a 0.4% MDR on UPI merchant transactions above ₹2,000 from October 15, paid by the merchant and not the consumer. Option A confuses it with merchant cash credit interest, C inverts who pays whom, and D wrongly ties it to a priority-sector lending rate cap.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Why charging for UPI changes the math
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: Merchant Discount Rate. Nearly identical to UPSC 2019: 'Which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate?'

questions.stem: With reference to geothermal energy and carbon capture technologies, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Geothermal energy harnesses heat stored beneath the Earth's surface and is classified as a renewable source of energy.
Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS) technologies can convert captured carbon dioxide into a stable mineral (rock-like) form, a process known as mineralisation.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct. Iceland draws roughly 30% of its electricity from geothermal sources (a renewable source) alongside hydropower, and its Carbfix technology, discussed as a CCUS tool for India, converts captured CO2 into stone through mineralisation.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Iceland courts India for geothermal, CCUS, ‘carbon-to-stone’ technologies
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: renewable energy classification and CCUS technology, in the mould of recent current-affairs-anchored energy/environment questions.

questions.stem: With reference to conditions at the Moon's south pole, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Most locations on the Moon experience about a fortnight of sunlight followed by a fortnight of darkness.
The extremely low temperatures inside permanently shadowed craters near the Moon's poles are primarily due to subsurface volcanic activity rather than the absence of sunlight.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: at most lunar locations a fortnight of daylight follows a fortnight of darkness. Statement 2 is incorrect: the craters near the south pole are cold (below -200°C) because they never receive sunlight, not because of volcanic activity; these shadowed regions preserve water ice as a result.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Analysis: Why NASA wants to build a nuclear reactor on the moon
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: lunar south pole permanently shadowed regions and water ice, relevant to Chandrayaan-3 landing site current affairs.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding neutrinos. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Neutrinos are electrically neutral subatomic particles with a very small but non-zero mass.
The IceCube neutrino observatory is located in Antarctica and detects neutrinos using an array of sensors buried deep in ice.
Neutrinos, being charged particles, get deflected by magnetic fields in interstellar space before reaching Earth.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: neutrinos are neutral with tiny mass, and IceCube is buried in Antarctic ice at the South Pole. Statement 3 is wrong — neutrinos are electrically neutral and travel in straight lines unaffected by magnetic fields; it is charged cosmic rays that get deflected, which is precisely why scientists turned to neutrinos to trace their cosmic origin.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Pioneer of IceCube neutrino detector wins 2026 Physics Nobel
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: properties of neutrinos and cosmic rays, triggered by the 2026 Physics Nobel for IceCube.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: EBV belongs to the herpesvirus family and spreads mainly through saliva.
The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) has classified EBV as a Group 1 carcinogen.
EBV, also known as human herpesvirus 4, has established causal links with Burkitt lymphoma and Hodgkin lymphoma.
Once a person is infected with EBV, the virus is completely cleared from the body within a few weeks.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct as stated in the IARC/WHO description of EBV. Statement 4 is false: after initial infection the virus remains in the body for life in a dormant state, kept in check by the immune system rather than being cleared.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: All you need to know about: Epstein-Barr virus
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: IARC carcinogen classification and viral oncogenesis, similar to past questions on WHO/IARC disease classifications.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of diseases and their causative agent/classification. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis
Classified as a Group 1 carcinogen by the IARC
Caused by Mycobacterium leprae and classified as a protozoal disease
Caused primarily by Epstein-Barr virus infection
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched: plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, IARC classifies EBV as Group 1 carcinogen, and EBV causes infectious mononucleosis. Pair 3 is wrong: leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae, a bacterium, not a protozoan.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Break the chain: On leprosy in India
questions.pyqLink: Static concept: causative agents and classification of common infectious diseases, a recurring pairs-matched theme.
